text: Critical Role episodes are organized by campaign and year, including one-shots. The Vox Machina campaign began as the cast's home game from 2012 to 2017 and premiered on March 12, 2015, with a live broadcast on Geek & Sundry Twitch and YouTube, running until October 12, 2017, for 115 episodes. The show began in medias res with the characters regrouping in Emon after about six months apart, continuing where the home game left off. While adventures before the Kraghammer arc (2015) were not formally recorded, audio from the first session was released in the third episode of the podcast All Work No Play, and Liam O'Brien released a recording of the magic carpet discovery. Episode 36 includes a summary of pre-series history with artwork by Wendy Sullivan Green and voice-overs by the cast. The comic Critical Role: Vox Machina Origins adapts the group's pre-show game, and the animated series The Legend of Vox Machina adapts a canonical story from the pre-stream period. Campaign one's closed captions were transcribed by a fan group and added to YouTube versions by Geek & Sundry, with VODs later uploaded to Critical Role's official YouTube channel. The second campaign began on January 11, 2018, featuring the Mighty Nein on the continent of Wildemount, set about 20 years after Vox Machina's final battle against Vecna, during a time of high tension between the Dwendalian Empire and the Kryn Dynasty. Prior to a COVID-19-related hiatus, episodes were broadcast live, but since episode 100 of Campaign Two, they have been pre-recorded. In May 2021, the cast announced Campaign Two would end soon, though "the Mighty Nein's story wasn't finished," with the campaign having spanned 100 hours of battle, 440 slain villains, and 530 hours of dice-roll-driven adventuring, plus a 7-hour finale that aired on June 3, 2021, becoming the longest episode. The third campaign premiered on October 21, 2021, with a live simulcast in Cinemark Theatres alongside Twitch and YouTube, and has been pre-recorded since. It is set on the continent of Marquet, which was briefly visited during Vox Machina, and follows the party Bells Hells, who become involved in the mystery of the Apogee Solstice and Exandria's second moon Ruidus. The story begins immediately after Exandria Unlimited, which took place 10 years after Campaign Two. Several cast members reprise their roles from Exandria Unlimited. In August 2024, Mercer began seeding the return of previous campaign parties within arcs of Campaign Three; in October 2024, the cast reprised their roles as the Mighty Nein while also playing as Bells Hells; in November 2024, they reprised their roles as Vox Machina in an arc focused on destroying the Malleus Key. The finale aired on February 6, 2025, at over eight and a half hours, becoming the longest episode in the series. Campaign four premiered on October 2, 2025, with Brennan Lee Mulligan as game master, set in the new world of Aramán, not in Exandria, and using the 2024 revision of the 5th Edition D&D ruleset. The player cast includes Luis Carazo, Robbie Daymond, Aabria Iyengar, Whitney Moore, Alexander Ward, and the earlier primary cast, including Mercer. After the first four sessions, Mulligan split the players into three groups: the Soldiers, the Seekers, and the Schemers, and the campaign continued in a West Marches-style structure. Exandria Unlimited (ExU) is an anthology spin-off; the first season premiered on June 24, 2021, set in Emon on Tal'Dorei, 30 years after Campaign One and 10 years after Campaign Two, with Aabria Iyengar as game master. A two-part sequel, Exandria Unlimited: Kymal, was released in March 2022. The second season, Exandria Unlimited: Calamity, premiered on May 26, 2022, following heroes from the Age of Arcanum (1,500 years before the main series) attempting to prevent the Calamity. The third season, Exandria Unlimited: Divergence, premiered on February 13, 2025, focusing on mortals rebuilding after the Calamity, with Brennan Lee Mulligan as game master. The Re-Slayer's Take is an all-ages actual play podcast set in Exandria, featuring a group rejected from "The Slayer's Take," with Jasmine Bhullar, Jasper William Cartwright, Caroline Lux, and Jasmine Chiong as players, and George Primavera and Nick Williams as Dungeon Masters; the first season premiered on May 20, 2024, and the second on September 10, 2024. Wildemount Wildlings, a spin-off, premiered on April 3, 2025, as a three-episode limited series about teenage campers at the Wildemount Wildlings Camp for Adventuring Kids and their two Mighty Nein counselors, with players Eden Riegel, Aleks Le, Brennan Lee Mulligan, and Libe Barer, and Marisha Ray and Ashley Johnson reprising their Campaign Two roles as Beauregard Lionett and Yasha Nydoorin, with Sam Riegel as gamemaster. Critical Role has also produced many one-shots, short adventures within a single session. As of January 2025, seven are considered canonical. These include the recovery of Grog's soul in Pandemonium during the final episode of Vox Machina, events in 826 P.D. when Taryon Darrington recruits a new group for the Darrington Brigade in Wildemount, six months after the destruction of Lucien in 837 P.D. when Uk'otoa's minions steal the last Cloven Crystal and the Mighty Nein reunite to recover it, the regrouping of the Mighty Nein after the Apogee Solstice in 843 P.D. and the discovery that Trent Ikithon has escaped to seek revenge, and a series of interconnected one-shots set in Sydney and Melbourne Australia where the cast plays as main campaign characters facing a common threat. The first Daggerheart one-shot is set in Exandria, with the cast reprising their roles as Bells Hells. Other canonical one-shots include the marriage of Jester and Fjord. Other one-shots are set in Exandria or feature established characters but are not canonical. These include a group of misfits in a tavern near Jorenn Village, a "Trinket's Honey Heist" using the one-page Honey Heist RPG system, a 4x4 Battle Royale between Vox Machina and the Mighty Nein at level 15, a Plunder Games battle where warriors from different timelines fight, with guests like Darin De Paul, Will Friedle, ND Stevenson, Sumalee Montano, and Anjali Bhimani reprising their roles, a Red Nose Day one-shot where Mercer runs an adventure for Stephen Colbert as Lucky Jack, joined by Mighty Nein members at level 5, with donors choosing game elements from March 23 to April 1, a one-shot following animal familiars, a Red Nose Day one-shot with Tony Hale and Sam Richardson joined by cast members in the Shattered Teeth, and a live non-canon one-shot with the Bells Hells pulled by Elemental Royals for a charity fundraiser benefiting the California Community Foundation (Wildfire Recovery Fund), the Latino Community Foundation, and the LA Fire Department Foundation after the January 2025 Southern California wildfires, with audience voting on which campaign characters to play. Some one-shots promote other intellectual properties, such as the promotional one-shot for Wendy's RPG system Feast of Legends, and others feature pre-release versions of the Daggerheart system, including episodes with The Menagerie adventuring party described as a "one-shot-turned-short-campaign" that demonstrated Daggerheart's open beta evolution. Some one-shots do not fit into any category, such as the escape of five students from detention at the magical school of Shmogwarts. Academics Lisa Horton and David Beard noted in The Routledge Handbook of Remix Studies and Digital Humanities that Critical Role's one-shots use pastiche and parody, such as mash-ups of Harry Potter with The Breakfast Club and Peter Pan with The Wizard of Oz, which are entertaining and generate positive fan response but are considered "unchallenging" and "uncomplicated" creative dead ends compared to the campaigns.
